items.title: Libye–Niger : Benghazi et Niamey scellent un accord de coopération stratégique…
items.description: Le Premier ministre nigérien, Ali Lamine Zeine, a été reçu ce dimanche 1er novembre 2026 à Benghazi par le général Saddam Haftar, vice-commandant en chef des forces armées libyennes, en présence du Dr Oussama Hammad, président du Conseil des ministres du gouvernement libyen. Il conduisait une importante délégation nigérienne composée de plusieurs responsables politiques et militaires. Cette rencontre a permis de réaffirmer la profondeur des liens historiques et culturels, ainsi que les relations de bon voisinage qui unissent la Libye et le Niger, deux pays et deux peuples frères. Le général Saddam Haftar a salué la solidité de ces relations et a transmis les salutations du maréchal Khalifa Haftar au président nigérien, le général Abdourahamane Tiani. De son côté, le Premier ministre Ali Lamine Zeine a exprimé sa satisfaction à l’issue de cette visite et a remercié les autorités libyennes pour l’accueil chaleureux et l’hospitalité réservés à sa délégation. Dans le cadre du renforcement des relations bilatérales et de l’élargissement de la coopération entre les deux pays dans divers domaines, les deux parties ont procédé à la signature d’un protocole d’accord de coopération stratégique entre la Libye et la République du Niger. Elles ont également souligné l’importance de poursuivre les consultations et la coordination, tout en veillant au suivi rigoureux de la mise en œuvre des engagements convenus, dans l’intérêt commun des deux nations et de leurs peuples. items.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire to end
items.description: A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine’s Kherson region, that has allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, is due to end on Sunday night. While the localised ceasefire on the front line has held since it was implemented last week, fighting has continued elsewhere. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power. Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said. Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia’s Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said. In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day. Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said. Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country. Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted. Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been “extremely high” over the past week, adding that Russia was “trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors”. He added that “every day” Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles – the only effective weapon for downing Russia’s deadly ballistic missiles – to the US, Europe and other partners. He thanked countries for their support so far and longer-term commitments, but called again for more immediate aid. On the front line, a localised ceasefire in the Kherson region was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday. The limited pause in hostilities, which started on Tuesday, was brokered with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo. It was originally confined to the city of Oleshky, which has been occupied by Russia since the first days of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and was expanded across the wider region of Kherson. Oleshky had been trapped on one side by the Dnipro river and the other by Russian forces, with routes out mined and subject to drone attack. Residents trapped there were suffering severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive. The truce allowed for Oleskhy residents to evacuate if they wanted, and there were emotional scenes on Saturday of reunions between loved ones who hadn’t seen eachother for years. There are Ukrainian military positions just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine’s northern border. The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman.

items.title: Conakry : Doumbouya inaugure Nimba Gold Refinery, une raffinerie d’or de 733 tonnes par an
items.description: CONAKRY- La Guinée dispose désormais d’une nouvelle infrastructure dédiée à la transformation de ses ressources aurifères. Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a procédé, ce dimanche 1er novembre 2026, à l’inauguration de la raffinerie d’or Nimba Gold Refinery, implantée dans la commune de Gbessia, à Conakry. La cérémonie a mobilisé plusieurs personnalités, dont le Premier ministre, Amadou Oury Bah, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Bouna Sylla, ainsi que des membres du gouvernement, des cadres de la présidence et différents acteurs du secteur minier. Cette installation industrielle ambitionne de donner à la Guinée les moyens de raffiner son or sur place et de tirer davantage de bénéfices économiques de l’exploitation de cette ressource naturelle. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Bouna Sylla, a présenté l’ouverture de cette raffinerie comme une avancée majeure pour l’industrie aurifère nationale. Il a notamment rappelé que, durant de nombreuses années, le pays exportait son or brut, sans capter une part suffisante de la valeur économique générée par son raffinage. « Depuis des siècles, la Guinée exploite et exporte son or à l’état brut. Si notre pays figure parmi les importants producteurs d’or en Afrique de l’Ouest, la valeur ajoutée générée par le raffinage ne profitait pas à notre économie. Aujourd’hui, cette époque est révolue », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le ministre, la mise en service de cette infrastructure devrait contribuer au renforcement de l’économie guinéenne, notamment grâce à la création d’emplois, au développement des compétences nationales et à l’accroissement des revenus tirés de l’exploitation de l’or. Bouna Sylla a également inscrit cette initiative dans le cadre du programme Simandou 2040, dont la vision accorde une place centrale à la transformation locale des ressources naturelles. « Cette raffinerie porte une ambition nationale : faire en sorte que l’or guinéen crée davantage de richesses en Guinée et pour les Guinéens. Notre ambition est de faire de la Guinée un hub régional de transformation des ressources minières et un modèle africain de création de valeur ajoutée à partir de nos ressources naturelles », a-t-il affirmé. Le ministre a, par ailleurs, évoqué les dispositions envisagées par les autorités pour consolider la filière aurifère. Il a annoncé que l’État prévoit d’acquérir, en francs guinéens, jusqu’à 30 % de la production des sociétés aurifères industrielles et semi-industrielles, conformément à la réglementation en vigueur. Cette mesure vise notamment à renforcer les réserves de change de la Banque centrale. Une capacité annuelle annoncée de 733 tonnes Au nom de Nimba Gold Refinery, Moussa Magassouba a exprimé sa satisfaction et sa reconnaissance lors de l’inauguration. Il a souligné l’importance stratégique de cette réalisation pour le développement industriel de la Guinée. Selon lui, la richesse minière du pays ne peut, à elle seule, garantir une prospérité durable si les ressources continuent d’être exportées sans transformation préalable. « Une nation riche en ressources minérales comme la nôtre ne peut durablement bâtir sa prospérité en se contentant d’extraire des substances brutes. Elle doit disposer des infrastructures, des technologies et des compétences nécessaires pour les transformer sur place. C’est exactement tout l’enjeu stratégique de ce grand projet de raffinerie », a-t-il expliqué. Moussa Magassouba a indiqué que Nimba Gold Refinery possède une capacité annuelle de raffinage de 733 tonnes. D’après les chiffres qu’il a avancés, même avec un taux d’utilisation limité à 50 % de sa capacité nominale, l’installation pourrait générer un flux financier annuel estimé à 4,5 milliards de dollars américains. Au-delà de ses performances industrielles annoncées, le responsable a mis l’accent sur les bénéfices attendus pour les populations guinéennes, particulièrement en matière d’emploi et de transfert de compétences. « Nous comptons créer des emplois qualifiés et durables pour les Guinéens, transférer des compétences techniques à notre jeunesse, développer des partenariats solides et renforcer la traçabilité de la filière. Nous savons que la confiance accordée par l’État et le peuple guinéen exige des résultats quotidiens », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également assuré que l’entreprise entend se conformer aux normes internationales et faire de la raffinerie une référence à l’échelle du continent africain. L’inauguration de Nimba Gold Refinery marque ainsi une nouvelle étape dans la stratégie guinéenne de valorisation des ressources minières. À travers cette infrastructure, les autorités entendent promouvoir la transformation locale de l’or, accroître les retombées économiques de son exploitation et renforcer la place de la Guinée dans la chaîne de valeur aurifère. items.title: MASI : la Bourse de Casablanca remet à plat ses règles
items.description: Après les secousses suscitées par la dernière révision annuelle, le Comité scientifique des indices rétablit provisoirement les anciens paramètres et lance une refonte complète du fonctionnement de l’indice, attendue sous un mois. Le Comité scientifique des indices de la Bourse de Casablanca s’est réuni le 30 octobre 2026 et a décidé d’engager une actualisation des règles de gestion de l’indice MASI. Dans un communiqué, la Bourse explique que cette démarche vise à tenir compte des évolutions liées au développement du marché et à l’arrivée de nouveaux émetteurs et investisseurs, tout en répondant aux sollicitations des acteurs de la place. Dans l’attente des nouvelles règles, une mesure transitoire est prise : les facteurs de flottant et de plafonnement redeviennent ceux qui étaient appliqués avant la révision annuelle du 29 octobre 2026. Selon le communiqué, cette actualisation répond à trois préoccupations. La première tient aux évolutions liées au développement du marché. La deuxième concerne l’arrivée de nouveaux émetteurs et de nouveaux investisseurs, qui transforme l’environnement dans lequel évolue l’indice. La troisième consiste à apporter une réponse aux sollicitations formulées par les acteurs du marché. La Bourse ne détaille pas ces demandes, mais elle présente la démarche comme une adaptation de l’indice à l’évolution de la place. Les nouvelles règles de gestion porteront notamment sur cinq points. Elles définiront d’abord les conditions et les modalités d’inclusion des nouvelles valeurs dans l’indice. Elles préciseront ensuite la méthodologie de calcul du flottant, puis les modalités d’actualisation des facteurs de flottant et de plafonnement. Le traitement des situations exceptionnelles figure également au programme, de même que les délais de publication des révisions de l’indice avant leur entrée en vigueur. L’emploi du terme « notamment » laisse entendre que cette liste n’est pas exhaustive. Le calendrier annoncé est serré. Ces travaux, menés dans le cadre du Comité des indices, seront finalisés dans un délai d’un mois. Les règles révisées qui en résulteront seront rendues publiques avant leur entrée en vigueur, afin de permettre à l’ensemble des acteurs de l’écosystème de s’y préparer. Le communiqué ne précise ni le contenu exact de ces règles ni leur date d’application. Il fixe en revanche un principe clair : la publication préalable, qui doit laisser aux intervenants le temps de s’organiser. Dans l’intervalle, la Bourse a choisi de ne pas laisser en place les paramètres issus de la dernière révision. Au nom de la stabilité et de la prévisibilité des modalités de gestion de l’indice, le Comité a décidé, à titre transitoire, de rétablir les facteurs de flottant et de plafonnement tels qu’ils étaient avant la révision annuelle du 29 octobre 2026. Ces facteurs sont ceux utilisés pour calculer les pondérations des différentes valeurs composant le MASI. La mesure s’appliquera jusqu’à l’entrée en vigueur des nouvelles règles de gestion, ce qui signifie que les pondérations de l’indice reposeront sur les anciens paramètres durant toute la période de transition. The post MASI : la Bourse de Casablanca remet à plat ses règles appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Dreams FC claim first league win after beating Basake Holy Stars
items.description: Dreams FC recorded their first win of the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League season with a 1-0 victory over Basake Holy Stars at the AAK II Sports Arena on Sunday, thanks to Bernard Kokonu’s second-half strike. The result ended Holy Stars’ unbeaten home run and gave Winfred Dormon’s side a much-needed boost after a difficult start to the campaign. The hosts played most of the game with 10 men after Bismark Teye was sent off in the 33rd minute following a fiercely contested first half. Dreams capitalised on their numerical advantage after the break, with Kokonu finding the net in the 50th minute to put the visitors ahead. The visitors held on to their lead for the remaining 40 minutes to secure all three points. The defeat leaves Holy Stars 10th in the league table. Abdulai Gazale’s side will look to return to winning ways when they travel to face Port City in their next fixture. Dreams remain bottom of the table despite the victory but will hope to build on the result when they host newly promoted Debibi United.

items.title: Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list
items.description: …Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action By Anayo Okoli The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent. The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation. Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council. In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition. The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation. “The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests. “We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said. The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties. It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good. While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests. “We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said. The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added. items.title: Sahara : l’ancien chef de la MINURSO appelle à mettre fin à la mission onusienne
items.description: Julian Harston, ancien chef de la Mission des Nations unies au Sahara (MINURSO), a appelé à mettre fin à la mission onusienne, estimant qu’elle est devenue obsolète et appartient désormais à une autre étape politique. Selon lui, la plupart des conditions qui avaient justifié la création de cette mission et défini son mandat initial ne correspondent plus à la réalité actuelle du différend autour du Sahara. Dans une publication sur son compte LinkedIn, Harston a affirmé que l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara n’avait jamais constitué une option réalisable depuis le départ. Il a également ajouté que le cessez-le-feu n’avait été accepté ni par le Front Polisario ni par l’Algérie, ce qu’il considère comme un indicateur des limites des justifications avancées pour maintenir la mission onusienne. L’ancien responsable des Nations unies a vivement critiqué l’Algérie, l’accusant d’avoir joué un rôle d’obstruction pendant de nombreuses années et d’avoir exploité différentes occasions pour s’opposer aux efforts de règlement du différend. Il lui a également reproché de maintenir des milliers de Sahraouis dans les camps de Tindouf, dans des conditions qu’il a qualifiées d’insupportables, sous la direction d’une direction qu’il a décrite comme vieillissante. Les positions de Harston revêtent une importance particulière au regard de son expérience directe dans la gestion de ce dossier. Il a occupé les fonctions de représentant spécial du secrétaire général des Nations unies au Sahara et de chef de la MINURSO du 5 février 2007 au 12 octobre 2009, soit près de deux ans et huit mois. Parallèlement à son appel à mettre fin à la mission de la MINURSO, Harston a exprimé son soutien sans équivoque à l’initiative d’autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine, qu’il a qualifiée de seule solution au différend. Il a affirmé que la communauté internationale soutenait cette option, appelant les Nations unies à adopter la même position. Ces déclarations interviennent dans le sillage des derniers développements au Conseil de sécurité, après que la Russie a opposé son veto, vendredi 30 octobre 2026, au projet de résolution américain relatif au renouvellement du mandat de la MINURSO. L’expiration du mandat de la mission soulève désormais des interrogations quant à l’avenir de sa présence onusienne et à la poursuite du processus de gestion du différend. The post Sahara : l’ancien chef de la MINURSO appelle à mettre fin à la mission onusienne appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Stop opposition politics, integrate with FG, Soludo tells South-East leaders
items.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government. Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka. The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party. The governor said that the coalition of political parties in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election represented a new direction for the region’s political engagement. According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre. He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president. He argued that the 5,000 votes Tinubu received in Anambra in the 2023 presidential election had contributed to attracting significant projects to the state and the region. “If 5,000 votes could attract these projects to our state and the region, imagine what would happen if we mobilised the electorate to give him massive support,” he said. On the economic reforms of the government, Soludo acknowledged efforts to stabilise foreign exchange availability and address fiscal challenges, noting that, although progress had been made, more work was required. He called for structural realignment of the coalition, saying existing campaign and mobilisation structures would be streamlined during the week. The governor urged grassroots mobilisers to adopt door-to-door campaigns, drawing lessons from successful political mobilisation strategies used during the 1983 elections. He also advised campaign teams not to be distracted by opposition criticism and verbal attacks on social media, but to remain focused on communicating what he described as the truth. Soludo reaffirmed his commitment to long-term governance, saying that the decisions being taken by his administration were aimed at securing a prosperous future for generations to come. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Mr Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as a landmark in the political history of Anambra. Ezeokenwa said that the coalition was an unprecedented political alignment involving different parties united in support of Tinubu’s re-election. He commended Soludo for providing leadership and facilitating the alliance, assuring that APGA would fully support the governor’s political direction. “Our party structure is ready to execute the instructions and deliver results at the polls,” he said. Also speaking, APC Chairman in Anambra, Sen. Emma Anosike, expressed appreciation for the development strides in the state. Anosike said that the political realignment was aimed at positioning Anambra more directly within the government’s political and developmental framework. He called for cooperation and solidarity among political parties, irrespective of their differences, to achieve the objectives of the coalition. The post Stop opposition politics, integrate with FG, Soludo tells South-East leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Qui ose gagne : le GPL, la prochaine frontière du secteur aval en Afrique
items.description: L’investissement dans le GPL représente la grande opportunité qui définira le secteur aval africain au cours des deux prochaines décennies. La fenêtre d’action est ouverte dès maintenant. Lors du premier Sommet de l’AIE sur la cuisson propre en Afrique, organisé à Paris en mai 2024, Akinwumi Adesina, alors président de la Banque africaine de développement, a évoqué ses souvenirs d’études à la lumière de lampes enfumées et de feux de cuisson, auxquels il associe des problèmes de vue. Aujourd’hui encore, près d’un milliard d’Africains cuisinent au bois de chauffage et au charbon de bois. La pollution de l’air domestique tue environ 815 000 Africains chaque année. Entre 2022 et 2023, la population de l’Afrique subsaharienne a augmenté de 30 millions de personnes, tandis que seulement 11 millions ont eu accès à des modes de cuisson propres. Pendant une décennie, le raffinage a dominé le récit du secteur aval africain. Mais la prochaine frontière est le gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL) : le produit pétrolier qui connaît la croissance la plus rapide sur le continent, un pilier de la cuisson propre et un marché dont la chaîne d’approvisionnement reste insuffisamment développée. Des investissements urgents sont nécessaires, depuis le traitement du gaz et les terminaux d’importation jusqu’aux centres d’embouteillage, à la logistique intérieure et aux bouteilles destinées aux ménages. La prochaine phase de croissance de l’Afrique sera façonnée non seulement par ceux qui disposent des ressources, mais aussi par ceux qui investiront les premiers dans les infrastructures reliant l’offre à la demande. LA COURSE À LA CONSTRUCTION DE L’AVENIR DU GPL EN AFRIQUE Le GPL représente 76 % des personnes qui accèdent à la cuisson propre en Afrique subsaharienne. Pourtant, la région a consommé 6,4 millions de tonnes en 2025, soit 4,8 kg par habitant, contre plus de 50 kg en Afrique du Nord. La demande a progressé de 12 % l’année dernière, et CITAC Africa prévoit qu’elle sera presque multipliée par trois pour atteindre 17 millions de tonnes d’ici 2045. D’ici 2050, une personne sur quatre dans le monde sera africaine. La chaîne d’approvisionnement n’est pas prête. Les États-Unis sont le premier fournisseur de GPL de l’Afrique, mais aucun terminal d’Afrique subsaharienne ne peut décharger une cargaison complète d’un très grand méthanier (VLGC), soit environ 45 000 tonnes. Seules une vingtaine d’installations de stockage de GPL sur le continent ont une capacité d’au moins 10 000 tonnes, et les stocks couvrent généralement dix jours de demande ou moins. L’Afrique achète principalement sur le marché au comptant, en petites cargaisons coûteuses, sans contrats à long terme ni prévisibilité des prix. La demande n’est pas le facteur limitant. Ce sont les molécules, les terminaux, les bouteilles et les camions qui font défaut. En 2026, lorsque le détroit d’Ormuz a été fermé, les prix à l’importation en Afrique de l’Est et de l’Ouest ont bondi de 70 à 100 % au-dessus de leur moyenne de 2025. Lorsque le prix des recharges double ou que les dépôts sont à sec, les ménages retournent au charbon de bois. Le développement de la cuisson propre progresse à la vitesse de la chaîne d’approvisionnement en combustibles. L’OPPORTUNITÉ SUR L’ENSEMBLE DE LA CHAÎNE DE VALEUR Des investissements sont nécessaires à chaque maillon de la chaîne : dans le traitement du gaz et le raffinage afin de conserver davantage de GPL africain sur le continent, malgré des exportations d’environ 10 millions de tonnes par an ; dans des plateformes d’importation capables d’accueillir des VLGC et des capacités de stockage stratégique permettant de conclure des contrats à long terme ; dans des centres d’embouteillage et la fabrication de bouteilles afin de réduire les coûts pour les ménages ; dans la logistique intérieure destinée aux marchés enclavés ; et dans la distribution du dernier kilomètre grâce à la recirculation des bouteilles, aux petites bouteilles de 3 à 6 kg et aux systèmes de paiement à l’usage. L’AIE estime que l’accès universel à la cuisson propre en Afrique coûtera environ 2 milliards de dollars par an d’ici 2040, soit moins de 0,1 % des investissements énergétiques mondiaux. Le capital n’est pas rare ; ce sont les structures de financement bancables qui le sont. Trop souvent, les programmes financent uniquement le réchaud plutôt que l’ensemble de la chaîne. L’opportunité n’attendra pas : ceux qui agiront les premiers contribueront à façonner l’avenir du GPL en Afrique. Trois questions sont essentielles : qui investira, où et comment réunir les promoteurs de projets et les financiers ? QUI DEVRAIT INVESTIR, ET POURQUOI ? Aucun acteur ne peut y parvenir seul, mais chacun a un rôle à jouer et une raison d’agir. Les producteurs américains fournissent la majeure partie des cargaisons. Des contrats à long terme, assortis de formules de prix sur 12 à 24 mois ou davantage, peuvent rendre les plateformes d’importation bancables, idéalement avec une participation minoritaire au capital. Les producteurs sécurisent ainsi une région où la demande de GPL progressera pendant des décennies. Le département américain de l’Énergie soutient l’initiative Fueling Lives, qui promeut l’accès au GPL à l’étranger. Les négociants internationaux tels que Petredec, Vitol et Trafigura disposent des capacités maritimes, de la gestion des risques et des bilans nécessaires pour exploiter des plateformes couvrant plusieurs pays. Le regroupement et la redistribution des cargaisons sont au cœur de leur activité ; les premiers à se lancer peuvent sécuriser des emplacements portuaires de premier choix. Les partenaires du Golfe, notamment les compagnies pétrolières nationales, les fonds souverains et les organismes de financement du commerce, peuvent apporter des capitaux et financer les cargaisons tout en bénéficiant de la croissance du secteur aval. Le programme Oil Sustainability Program de l’Arabie saoudite soutient la cuisson propre au GPL par l’intermédiaire de Forward7, notamment du défi IGNITE. Les organismes saoudiens de financement du commerce peuvent financer les cargaisons. L’étape suivante consiste à mobiliser des capitaux pour les infrastructures. Les investisseurs chinois sont déjà à la table des négociations. En avril, la NNPC a signé un protocole d’accord avec Sanjiang Chemical et Xinganchen (Fuzhou) Industrial Park concernant un éventuel partenariat en capital visant à redémarrer et à développer les raffineries de Port Harcourt et de Warri, notamment les activités pétrochimiques et les pôles industriels fondés sur le gaz. Les entreprises chinoises peuvent nouer des partenariats dans le traitement du gaz, la pétrochimie et la fabrication de bouteilles, à condition que le butane de qualité cuisson soit réservé aux cuisines africaines. Les compagnies pétrolières nationales africaines apportent des terrains portuaires, des concessions, du gaz domestique et des partenariats avec les pays hôtes, tout en renforçant la sécurité énergétique grâce au gaz actuellement torché ou exporté. Les distributeurs africains tels qu’Oryx Energies, Sahara, Ardova et Rainoil connaissent les clients, les régulateurs et les itinéraires intérieurs. Oryx, désormais dirigée par des Africains à la suite du récent rachat par l’équipe de direction, est un acteur majeur de la commercialisation du GPL. En Tanzanie, l’entreprise a inauguré en 2024 le premier terminal d’importation de GPL de Zanzibar. À notre connaissance, les investissements de ces distributeurs dans le dernier kilomètre ont porté leurs fruits. Le modèle proposé est celui d’un consortium de plateformes régionales : un négociant comme opérateur, des contrats d’approvisionnement américains comme socle, une compagnie pétrolière nationale africaine comme partenaire du pays hôte, des financements du Golfe ou des institutions de développement, et des distributeurs africains au service des marchés intérieurs et du dernier kilomètre. OÙ INVESTIR, ET POURQUOI ? MARCHÉS D’ANCRAGE : L’ÉCHELLE AUJOURD’HUI Le Nigeria, la Côte d’Ivoire, l’Afrique du Sud et l’Angola représentent plus de la moitié de la demande de l’Afrique subsaharienne. Le Nigeria, avec environ 1,4 million de tonnes, vise 5 millions de tonnes par an d’ici 2030. À mesure que la raffinerie Dangote remplace les importations, les possibilités se déplacent vers le traitement du gaz, le stockage, l’embouteillage et la distribution. La Côte d’Ivoire a enregistré une croissance de 12 % en 2025 et l’Afrique du Sud de 15 % ; Durban se dote d’un terminal de 30 000 tonnes, avec une plateforme ferroviaire prévue pour le Gauteng. L’Angola, exportateur net doté du plus récent grand terminal d’Afrique, à Barra do Dande, peut devenir un fournisseur régional. PLATEFORMES DE CORRIDOR : UN TERMINAL, PLUSIEURS MARCHÉS Les plateformes côtières peuvent desservir les pays voisins enclavés. Le Kenya (Mombasa) peut approvisionner l’Ouganda, le Rwanda, le Soudan du Sud et l’est de la RDC ; Taifa Gas achève la construction d’un terminal capable d’accueillir des VLGC, tandis que la consommation kenyane reste environ deux fois inférieure à son objectif de 15 kg par habitant. La Tanzanie peut desservir la Zambie, le Malawi, le Burundi et la RDC ; le terminal de Tanga de Petredec, capable d’accueillir des VLGC, doit entrer en service en 2027. L’Angola peut atteindre la RDC et la Zambie par le corridor de Lobito. La Côte d’Ivoire et le Ghana sont des portes d’entrée vers le Sahel ; le Ghana vise un taux de pénétration du GPL de 50 % d’ici 2030. MARCHÉS FRONTIÈRES : LE PLUS GRAND POTENTIEL DE CROISSANCE La République démocratique du Congo et l’Éthiopie comptent plus de 250 millions d’habitants, mais n’ont consommé respectivement que 25 000 et 28 000 tonnes de GPL en 2025, à peine plus qu’une cargaison de VLGC à elles deux. Kinshasa fonctionne au charbon de bois. Celui qui construira les routes d’approvisionnement vers ces marchés les façonnera pour toute une génération. COMMENT L’ARDA RÉUNIT LES PROMOTEURS DE PROJETS ET LES FINANCIERS Les investissements multinationaux nécessitent une plateforme neutre réunissant les gouvernements, les régulateurs, les entreprises et les financiers. C’est le rôle de l’ARDA. À l’occasion de sa 20e année d’existence, avec environ 85 membres à travers l’Afrique, l’ARDA peut réunir autour d’une même table les partenaires de consortiums de plateformes régionales. Constituer un portefeuille de projets. Le Forum de l’investissement de l’ARDA évalue les projets selon cinq critères (durabilité, soutien réglementaire, viabilité économique, viabilité technique et capacité d’exécution), puis met les projets bancables en relation avec des financiers, notamment Afreximbank, l’Africa Finance Corporation, Standard Bank et la Mauritius Commercial Bank. Déployer les capitaux. Avec le Global LPG Partnership (GLPGP), l’ARDA fait avancer la création d’un fonds d’un milliard de dollars américains consacré à la cuisson propre. Elle mobilise les institutions africaines de financement du développement et ses membres afin de constituer un portefeuille de projets, les terminaux capables d’accueillir des VLGC constituant la première catégorie prioritaire. Réduire les risques du marché. À travers son Forum annuel sur le GPL, coorganisé cette année avec la World Liquid Gas Association, ainsi que ses groupes de travail sur le GPL, la réglementation et le financement durable, l’ARDA plaide en faveur de règles de sécurité harmonisées, de prix reflétant les coûts, d’un accès ouvert aux infrastructures partagées, de stocks minimaux et de contrats types. L’ARDA préconise également un recours accru aux garanties partielles de risque, qui ne représentent que 5 % du financement public international de l’énergie propre destiné aux pays en développement. Partager les données et les partenariats. Avec CITAC, Argus, S&P Global, la World Liquid Gas Association et l’AIE, l’ARDA fournit des données de marché pour dimensionner les projets et éviter les surcapacités lorsque l’offre intérieure remplace les importations. Elle met ses membres en relation avec Fueling Lives et Forward7, partage des études de cas et relie les distributeurs et les innovateurs du dernier kilomètre aux dispositifs de soutien. QUI OSE GAGNE Les premiers acteurs prennent déjà position, et les capitaux chinois s’intéressent aux raffineries et au gaz du Nigeria. Washington et Riyad, capitales de deux des principaux pays exportateurs de GPL au monde, défendent la cuisson propre en Afrique, mais les investissements dans des terminaux à grande échelle n’ont pas suivi. C’est là que réside l’opportunité. Les sites portuaires, les concessions et les clients d’ancrage sont en nombre limité. Les investisseurs qui agissent maintenant peuvent sécuriser des terminaux, des contrats et des relations avec les clients sur un marché appelé à tripler. Ceux qui attendent risquent de trouver les meilleurs sites déjà occupés. Le combustible est disponible et la demande est certaine. Alors, qui veillera à ce que la prochaine génération puisse étudier à la lumière d’un éclairage propre et manger des repas cuisinés sans fumée ? Rejoignez les leaders du secteur au troisième Forum sur le GPL de l’ARDA, à Dar es Salaam, les 24 et 25 novembre 2026, autour du thème « Libérer le potentiel du GPL en Afrique : un catalyseur de l’industrialisation, de la sécurité énergétique et d’une transition énergétique inclusive », afin d’examiner qui saisira cette opportunité et transformera le potentiel du GPL africain en investissements, en retombées concrètes et en un avenir plus sain pour tous. Qui ose… gagne. Le moment, c’est maintenant. Anibor O. Kragha, Secrétaire exécutif de l’African Refiners and Distributors Association (ARDA)

items.title: 2027: Otti warns supporters against disrupting opposition campaigns
items.description: Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights. Otti said anyone found obstructing rival political parties from holding lawful rallies or other campaign activities would face arrest, irrespective of party affiliation. The governor gave the warning on Sunday in Umuahia while flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he stressed that political competition must be conducted within the confines of the law. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said. Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed. He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. He urged opposition parties to examine available performance data before making claims about the state, citing its ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations. “You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said. The governor also cited feedback from Abians at home and abroad, as well as development opportunities offered by multilateral institutions, as indications of progress under his administration. “It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he said. Otti thanked residents for attending the campaign flag-off and urged Labour Party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the state. “This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added. The event featured the presentation of party flags to Labour Party candidates for the 2027 National and State Houses of Assembly elections. Party members, candidates and supporters attended the ceremony, chanting solidarity songs in support of their respective candidates. items.title: Baseball5 : la Türkiye enfonce les Lionceaux
items.description: Le parcours du Sénégal dans le tournoi de Baseball5 des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 tourne à la désillusion. Après deux premières défaites contre le Taipei chinois et Cuba, les Lionceaux ont été dominés par la Türkiye, ce dimanche 1er novembre, lors de leur troisième sortie dans le groupe A. Face à une formation turque déterminée à terminer le premier tour sur une bonne note, les représentants sénégalais n'ont pas réussi à inverser la tendance. Cette nouvelle déconvenue vient confirmer les difficultés rencontrées par l'équipe nationale dans une compétition où le niveau technique et l'expérience des adversaires ont mis à rude épreuve les jeunes joueurs sénégalais. Avec trois défaites en autant de sorties, le Sénégal termine la phase de groupes sans victoire. items.title: NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal
items.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term. Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President. Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years. Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges. He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty. “While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years. “He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said. He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living. “What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected. “Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said. The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion. He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership. items.title: Biennale de Luanda : Euphrasie Kouassi Yao plaide pour le leadership des femmes dans la gestion de l’eau
items.description: La ministre-conseillère spéciale du Premier ministre ivoirien chargée du Genre, Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, a pris part, les 22 et 23 octobre 2026, à la 4ᵉ Biennale de Luanda, en Angola. Elle y a défendu l'intégration du genre dans la gouvernance de l’eau comme un levier de prévention des conflits et de consolidation de la paix en Afrique. Plus de 1 000 participants venus de 62 pays ont pris part à la 4ᵉ Biennale de Luanda, consacrée à la culture de la paix et de la non-violence. Organisée avec l’appui de l’Union africaine et de l’UNESCO, cette rencontre a porté sur le thème : « Renforcer la gouvernance de l’eau en Afrique comme outil de prévention, de médiation et de résolution des conflits ». Invitée par l’UNESCO, la titulaire de la Chaire UNESCO « Eau, Femmes et Pouvoir de Décisions » (CUEFPOD), Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, a mis en avant l’importance de la participation des femmes aux instances de décision relatives à la gestion de l’eau. À travers l’exemple du village de Diatokro, en Côte d’Ivoire, elle a montré comment l’implication des femmes dans la gestion d’une pompe hydraulique a contribué à réduire les pannes, à améliorer l’accès à l’eau et à renforcer la cohésion communautaire depuis 23 ans. Pour la ministre ivoirienne, la paix se construit au quotidien grâce à des actions concrètes et à l’engagement des communautés. Elle a également présenté le programme CREA-PAIX (Communautés Régionales pour l’Autonomisation et la Paix), qui mobilise plus de 3 000 bénévoles dans 27 pays autour de la prévention communautaire des conflits et de la promotion de la non-violence active. Au terme des travaux, la Déclaration de Luanda 2026 a notamment recommandé le renforcement de la coopération autour des bassins transfrontaliers, la mobilisation de financements innovants et une plus grande implication des femmes et des jeunes dans les décisions relatives à l’eau. En marge de la Biennale, Euphrasie Kouassi Yao a échangé avec le directeur général de l’UNESCO, Khaled El-Enany. Elle lui a présenté les initiatives ivoiriennes en faveur de l’égalité des chances, notamment la stratégie Genre et Développement et le Compendium des compétences féminines de Côte d’Ivoire (COCOFCI), tout en plaidant pour leur valorisation à l’échelle africaine. items.title: 2027: Akpabio predicts highest South-South votes for Tinubu from Akwa Ibom
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election. Akpabio made the declaration on Sunday during a special church service at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, organised to dedicate the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 election campaigns to God. The service had the theme, “We Are Well Able”. In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, the Senate President said Akwa Ibom indigenes, particularly APC members, must close ranks and present a united front to ensure the party’s success at the polls. He said the state had a responsibility to reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given him by mobilising votes for the President. According to him, the support of Tinubu contributed to his emergence as Senate President, making him the number three citizen in the country. “Whether you like him or not, he is there today. The only way to thank Mr President for that support is to give him all our votes. “From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said. In an address titled, “One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God”, Akpabio said while the people acknowledged God’s sovereignty over their individual and collective destinies, they must also uphold righteousness, justice and mercy. He described Akwa Ibom as a Nigerian success story, attributing its progress to purposeful leadership, peace and development. The Senate President said development should not be measured only by roads and buildings but also by the bridges built between people and the hope restored in their lives. He urged political leaders and party members to sustain the state’s progress and ensure that its future achievements surpassed those already recorded. On party unity, Akpabio cautioned against divisions between old and new members of the APC, insisting that all members should be treated equally. “In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility,” he said. Using a biblical reference from John 14:2, he said there was room for everyone in the party, regardless of when they joined or their political standing. He added that political ambitions should not override the welfare of the people, urging party members to conduct their campaigns in ways that respect human dignity. Akpabio further said the development of Akwa Ibom was inseparable from the progress of Nigeria, stressing that the state could not remain indifferent to insecurity and hardship in other parts of the country. “Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom contributes,” he said. Earlier, Governor Umo Eno thanked the people for their support during the last election and appealed for increased support for Tinubu, Akpabio, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Eno also pledged to continue serving the people with the fear of God if given another mandate. items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
items.description: Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least eight people, including a child, according to hospitals, despite a year-old ceasefire. In Gaza City to the north, hospital officials said a missile attack hit a group of civilians next to Cairo School in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood, killing three people, including a four-year-old boy. In the southern city of Khan Younis, the Hamas-run ministry of interior said a drone attack targeted a group of police officers in the Al-Mawasi area, killing five, as they were carrying out their routine duties. The Israeli military said it had carried out two attacks on what it described as military operatives but has not yet provided evidence or further information. Outside Gaza City’s Shifa Hospital, video showed a crowd of men gathered to pray next to two body bags and the tiny body of the child, which was wrapped in a white towel. “My son and his child were martyred. They were sitting in their tent, bothering no one, and nothing else was happening in the area when suddenly, a missile struck them, and they were martyred,” Ali Oweis told AFP news agency. “There is no ceasefire; the war is ongoing — don’t you see?” At Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, women despaired as body bags lay on the floor, video showed. The interior ministry named the five police officers killed, who were between the ages of 23 and 53, and called the attack a “horrific massacre”. A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day. Since then, 1,580 people have been killed, according to Gaza’s Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says it is targeting Hamas, but often civilians are also killed. Meanwhile, a peace plan for Gaza, brokered by the Trump administration, has stalled. The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for all of the 48 remaining hostages held in Gaza, and an agreement to end the war – which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage. Since the war began, 74,594 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory’s health ministry.

items.title: Anambra coalition is battle for Nigeria’s soul – Soludo
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the political coalition formed by parties in the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a battle for the soul of Nigeria and Ndigbo. Soludo, who is the Anambra State Coordinator of Tinubu’s re-election campaign, spoke on Sunday during the inauguration of the presidential campaign structure at the International Convention Centre, Awka. He said the coalition, which brings together political leaders across party lines, was formed primarily to secure Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that Ndigbo must actively participate in national politics rather than remain on the sidelines. The governor described the forthcoming political contest as a clash between emotion and reason, expressing the view that emotional politics could only dominate temporarily before giving way to strategic calculations. Addressing candidates contesting other elective positions on different party platforms, Soludo assured them of a level playing field, but stressed that the coalition’s common objective was to ensure Tinubu’s return to office. He recalled that prominent Igbo political leaders, including Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, Dr. Alex Ekwueme and Dr. Chuba Okadigbo, played significant roles in national politics, insisting that the South-East could not afford to isolate itself from developments at the centre. According to him, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, recognised the importance of national political engagement and consequently resolved to align with the Federal Government. He said APGA and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, shared progressive ideals anchored on federalism and shared prosperity, adding that Tinubu understood the need for progressives to work together for national development. Reflecting on his political journey, which he said began in 1980 under the principle of “one nation, one destiny”, Soludo urged Ndigbo to consider their long-term political and economic interests. He argued that state revenues alone could not adequately finance major infrastructure such as federal rail lines and gas pipelines without strategic partnerships with the Federal Government. The governor also noted that despite Tinubu securing about 5,000 votes in Anambra State during the 2023 presidential election, his administration had extended support to the state. He expressed optimism that greater federal interventions could come if more people in Anambra supported the President in the next election. Soludo called for an end to what he described as opposition and protest politics practised in the state since 2015, urging Ndigbo to embrace active participation in governance at the national level. He further argued that a fragmented opposition would find it difficult to defeat an incumbent president, adding that his assessment was informed by his claimed record of correctly predicting presidential election outcomes in Nigeria since 1983. On the future of presidential power rotation, Soludo said that following the completion of the South’s second term, power was expected to return to the North before rotating back to the South around 2039. He urged Ndigbo to position themselves within the national political structure ahead of that period. On political differences within Anambra, the governor said he maintained cordial personal and family relationships with political opponents, stressing that their disagreements were limited to political strategies and ideologies. He also acknowledged federal fiscal interventions aimed at improving foreign exchange availability for importers, noting that although progress had been made, more work remained. Outlining the campaign’s next steps, Soludo said political structures across the state would be streamlined before the end of the following week. He maintained that elections were won at polling units and ward levels, urging supporters to remain focused despite criticism and verbal attacks on social media. In his remarks, the APC state chairman, Senator Emma Anosike, said he had initially been sceptical about the meeting but expressed appreciation for what he described as the developmental strides recorded in Anambra. Anosike said the coalition was intended to ensure the state’s direct participation in national governance. He called for unity among party members, while noting that candidates contesting on different platforms were free to demonstrate their individual political strengths. He, however, urged all stakeholders to work together towards Tinubu’s re-election. Also speaking, the APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as an unprecedented coalition united by the objective of securing Tinubu’s re-election. He commended Soludo for facilitating the political alignment and pledged the readiness of APGA’s structures to implement campaign directives and mobilise support for the President. The event attracted representatives of several political parties, including the PDP, Accord Party, APGA and APC, in what organisers described as a broad-based political alliance ahead of the 2027 presidential election. items.title: “He could no longer deliver” – Ten Hag explains why Ronaldo struggled at Man United
items.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has criticised Cristiano Ronaldo’s fitness and commitment during their time together at Old Trafford, saying the Portuguese forward could “no longer deliver” at the highest level after leaving Juventus in 2021. Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch club FC Twente, made the remarks during an interview with ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie on Sunday, reflecting on his strained relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner. Ronaldo returned to Manchester United from Juventus in 2021 and scored 27 goals in 54 appearances under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ten Hag. However, his relationship with the Dutch manager deteriorated as he was frequently left out of the starting line-up. United eventually terminated his contract in November 2022 following his explosive interview with Piers Morgan, in which he said he felt “betrayed” by Ten Hag and criticised the club’s hierarchy. Reflecting on the challenges of managing the forward, Ten Hag said Ronaldo’s reluctance to put the team first created problems within the squad. “The challenge is to get the team functioning, really as always. Every player is important in that and you need top players to be able to win. Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team. And that was simply the problem with Ronaldo.” He acknowledged Ronaldo’s influence among his teammates but insisted the forward’s performances had declined. “The players wanted to work for him and they looked up to him because let there be no misunderstanding about that. He is of course a tremendous player, one of the greats of all time. But that is also the reality over the last seven, eight years he simply can no longer deliver. From Juventus onwards it’s simply over. “And that is actually the great gift of Real Madrid — they always know when to say goodbye to players at the right moment. They recognise when a player’s level is declining and they say goodbye at a moment when to the outside world, they still appear to be at their peak. But they can no longer actually deliver.” Ronaldo was 36 when he returned to the Premier League, where his perceived inability to press opposition defenders attracted criticism from pundits and commentators. Ten Hag, however, argued that the issue went beyond the forward’s age, claiming he was no longer willing to push himself physically during training. “I naturally gave him a special status,” Ten Hag said. “I also went to him, I spoke to him prior to that job, I explained to him how we were going to play, what his role in that would be, what I expected of him, and what he could expect from me and from the team. But ultimately you also have to deliver yourself and he was no longer capable of pushing himself to the limit. “As I just said, he could no longer bring himself to push through the pain, to give everything every single day and to train at his maximum in order to get fit. And if you’re not fit in the Premier League, Champions League, or with the Portuguese national team, well, then you simply have no chance.” Asked about Ronaldo’s reputation for exceptional dedication to physical fitness, Ten Hag said the perception did not entirely reflect the situation during their time together. “That’s not entirely true, but that is the image. And that is of course how he became so good. But ultimately he could no longer bring himself to do that. “If you can’t do it, well, then the laws of the Premier League are merciless. Then you can no longer keep up, you are no longer able to get into the box. He can still finish a chance, you still see that. But to get into that power and intensity of the Premier League, that’s no longer possible. For that you need to be fit.” The former United manager also dismissed suggestions that Ronaldo’s goals had changed his assessment of the forward’s performances, saying the player arrived late for pre-season preparations. “That didn’t happen because he arrived very late due to personal circumstances. By then the season had already started and things went wrong straight away. He wasn’t fit and couldn’t deliver.” Despite his criticism, Ten Hag praised Ronaldo’s contribution to football but maintained that he had to make decisions in the interest of Manchester United. He also compared the forward’s approach to that of Argentina captain Lionel Messi, arguing that even the greatest players must prioritise their teams. “No one is bigger than a club or a country,” Ten Hag said. “Not even Cristiano Ronaldo and not even Messi. In the end, the team always comes first. And so, as I just said, every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must yield to the team. And if he no longer does that, well then it can’t be a success and it will never become a success. Then it simply stops. “That is also what’s remarkable about Messi — how he worked at Argentina. That was fantastic to see. But that also required a big investment from Messi himself. Ultimately everyone went along with it and everyone worked for him but he of course gave an enormous amount back.” Ten Hag’s latest comments come after Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese Football Federation following his walkout on the national team during the October international break. He was also fined €255 but has indicated his willingness to represent Portugal again. The Dutchman also addressed his departure from Manchester United, dismissing suggestions of bitterness towards the club. Asked whether restrictions surrounding his exit had prevented him from speaking publicly for two years, Ten Hag said: “I was allowed to give interviews, but not to damage the club. But I wouldn’t have done that anyway — that goes without saying. “United gave me so much and I worked there with such great pleasure, with the people. [We] simply had a fantastic relationship, built fantastic connections. And the fans, such fantastic moments in those FA Cup finals, League Cup, [they] always supported. So there’s no bitterness.” Vanguard News The post “He could no longer deliver” – Ten Hag explains why Ronaldo struggled at Man United appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mauritanie: une campagne de dons lancée sur TikTok a permis en quelques heures de récolter 100 millions d’anciennes ouguiyas pour les malades
items.description: Des activistes mauritaniens ont récolté 100 millions MRO sur la plateforme TikTok en moins de 12 heures, dans le cadre d’une campagne de dons lancée dimanche matin par le créateur de contenu Sidi Al-Sadat, dans le but d’aider des patients démunis, notamment des personnes atteintes d’un cancer ou d’une maladie rénale, à couvrir les frais de leur traitement. Les dons ont été collectés lors d’un direct sur la plateforme, auquel des centaines de Mauritaniens ont participé en versant des contributions financières, jusqu’à atteindre un montant total de 100 millions d’anciennes ouguiyas. Il s’agit de l’une des plus importantes campagnes de dons jamais organisées sur les réseaux sociaux du pays en termes de volume de contributions sur une période aussi courte. Ce n’était pas la première campagne menée par les « Al-Sadat » en collaboration avec d’autres militants sur la plateforme car elles avaient déjà organisé des collectes de fonds pour des Mauritaniens vivant dans des conditions précaires, dont certaines ont abouti à l’achat de maisons pour des familles qui vivaient auparavant dans des cabanes. Elles ont également récolté des fonds pour aider des malades à se déplacer et à recevoir des soins. Ces initiatives s’appuient sur des diffusions en direct et l’interaction avec les abonnés pour mobiliser les dons ; les donateurs effectuent leurs versements en quelques heures, dans le cadre d’une forme d’action caritative dont la portée s’est élargie via les réseaux sociaux en Mauritanie. La dernière campagne a suscité un vif intérêt sur les réseaux sociaux, où des blogueurs et des militants ont salué la participation de centaines de donateurs à la collecte de fonds, ainsi que cette initiative visant à aider les malades démunis, alors que beaucoup font face à des difficultés financières pour couvrir les frais de traitement.

items.title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
items.description: Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney’s streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year’s deadly shooting at Bondi Beach. The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles – an unfamiliar sight for most residents. New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship “to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents”. Fifteen people – including a 10-year-old girl – were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach. The attack was Australia’s worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech. One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was “unnerving”. “They are just everywhere. Those guns are huge.” But another woman told the broadcaster that seeing police with weapons made her feel safe. ARC is specifically designed to be “highly visible across Sydney, driving specialist vehicles and carrying rifles,” New South Wales police said in a statement. Its role “is built on a simple principle – preserving life,” Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said. The shooting on 14 December put huge pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s government, with calls for immediate action on antisemitism. Jewish communities have welcomed the new police operation, which will eventually consist of 250 officers, but others have called for safeguards to protect human rights. “No Australian wants to see officers with military weapons on our streets, but the sight of body bags is far worse,” Alex Ryvchin, co-CEO of Executive Council of Australian Jewry, said. But Amnesty International Australia said it was concerned about the “militarisation of policing”, and asked for assurances from the state government that ARC will not be used to suppress peaceful protests. “Any expansion of police powers and capabilities must be accompanied by clear, publicly accessible rules, robust independent oversight and accountability,” said the organisation’s Andrew Witheford. The New South Wales administration defended the new measures. “Our world changed forever. That’s just the truth of it, right across this country. And I said it at the time, we will never be the same again,” the state’s Police Minister Yasmin Catley told the ABC. One of the alleged gunmen, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 78 offences including 15 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and one count of committing a terrorist act. His father, Sajid Akram, 50 – who was also armed and shot at the crowd on Bondi Beach – was killed by police at the scene.

items.title: National Service Authority sets November 2 for military training screening
items.description: The National Service Authority (NSA) has announced that screening and medical examinations for preselected National Service Personnel (NSPs) who expressed interest in participating in the Basic Military Training Programme will begin on Monday, November 2, 2026. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : les Lioncelles de Futsal écrasent les Fidji (8-1)
items.description: L’équipe nationale féminine de futsal du Sénégal a signé une entrée en matière remarquable aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. items.title: Oye laments rising hardship, poverty despite higher revenue for FG, States
items.description: …Calls for Measurable Results for Govt Spending, Says Revenue Gains Must Translate into Better Lives for Nigerians The Chairman of the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics, Dele Kelvin Oye, has called on the Federal and state governments to ensure that increased public revenues translate into better living conditions for Nigerians, noting that Nigeria’s fiscal positions have improved but yet to produce a level of citizen satisfaction that reflects the gains. Oye said governments must move beyond revenue generation and focus on delivering measurable improvements in public services, infrastructure and economic opportunities. He made the call while commenting on the revised 2026 State Performance Index (pSPI) by Phillips Consulting, which showed that despite improved fiscal conditions across parts of the federation, citizens’ experience of government performance remained only marginally positive. The report recorded a national composite citizen satisfaction score of 3.01 out of five, barely above the neutral midpoint of 3.00. Oye said the findings underscored the need for governments to demonstrate how increased revenues were improving the lives of citizens, rather than relying on budget figures and financial performance indicators. He noted that higher revenues should create room for governments to repair roads, improve water systems, equip health facilities, support businesses and strengthen education, adding that revenue was only a resource for development, not development itself. According to the report, finding employment recorded the lowest citizen rating at 2.31, placing it in the critical category. Clean water scored 2.67, government support for businesses 2.71, security 2.84, while law-enforcement conduct recorded 2.85. Oye said the figures reflected the everyday challenges confronting Nigerians and highlighted the gap between fiscal performance and the quality of public services. He cautioned that higher revenue could fail to produce meaningful development where funds were poorly allocated, released late, lost through weak procurement or spent on projects that were never completed or maintained. He said government budgets should therefore be assessed not only by the amount allocated or spent, but by the results achieved and the number of citizens who benefited. Oye called for the inclusion of measurable service-delivery outcomes in the assessment of government performance, including whether projects were completed on time and within budget, whether public facilities were functional and whether citizens experienced improvements after delivery. He also urged governments to publish transparent information on public spending, procurement, project completion and service outcomes to enable citizens to monitor how public funds were being used. The Alliance for Ethics chairman proposed that every state, the Federal Capital Territory and local government publish a 90-day public delivery plan focused on no more than three of its weakest service areas. He said the plans should contain clear targets, timelines, funding arrangements and publicly accessible monitoring systems, with governments required to explain missed milestones and publish corrective measures. Oye stressed that the proposed 90-day plans should serve as the first phase of a longer-term delivery programme, rather than promises to resolve complex challenges such as unemployment, insecurity or water access within three months. He said the objective was to ensure that citizens could track public funds from allocation to project completion and determine whether the resulting services were improving their lives. Oye further called for stronger coordination among the Federal, state and local governments, noting that challenges such as employment, public safety, water, sanitation and primary healthcare required cooperation across the different tiers of government. He said the Federal Government should provide a stable national economic environment and transparent funding arrangements, while state and local governments must ensure that resources within their control were efficiently managed and directed towards the needs of citizens. Oye maintained that stronger fiscal conditions offered governments an opportunity to improve public welfare, but insisted that the opportunity must be matched by transparency, accountability and effective use of public resources. He said the ultimate test of government performance was not the size of its revenue or budget, but the quality of life that public spending made possible for Nigerians. According to him, “Nigeria is at a crucial point in its public-finance journey. State governments have recently received and reported higher nominal revenues. That should create room to repair roads, improve water systems, equip health facilities, support enterprise and strengthen education. But revenue is not development; it is only the resource from which development may be built. “The revised 2026 pcl. State Performance Index (pSPI) puts this challenge in clear view. It records stronger fiscal conditions across parts of the federation, aided by larger Federation Account distributions, higher VAT receipts, exchange-rate effects and other national macroeconomic adjustments. Yet the report’s 2026 citizen survey records a national composite score of only 3.01 out of 5, just above its neutral midpoint of 3.00. “The conclusion should be sober. The figure does not prove that public services have not improved at all. It does show that stronger fiscal conditions have not yet translated into a level of citizen experience that commands broad confidence. Under the report’s own scale, satisfaction only marginally outweighs dissatisfaction.” He added, “Alliance for Ethics will treat the pSPI as a starting point for accountability, not a final judgment on any state. We will ask whether governments publish delivery compacts, make data usable, manage fiscal risks, complete projects, maintain public assets and respond to the services citizens rate most weakly. “Citizens, journalists, civil society and businesses should keep asking five questions: What exactly changed? Where is the independent evidence? Who benefited and who was left out? What did it cost, including future debt? Can the public inspect the result without an appointment, a press pass or special access? “Nigeria does not lack revenue headlines, plans or project announcements. What it needs is a more rigorous public ethic: money must be allocated well, released on time, spent transparently, converted into functioning services and measured by the change it produces in people’s lives. “The pSPI’s score of 3.01 is not a reason for despair. It is a reason for discipline. Higher nominal receipts create an opportunity; only effective utilisation and measurable outcomes create development. A government should be judged not only by the size of its budget, but by the quality of life its budget makes possible.” The post Oye laments rising hardship, poverty despite higher revenue for FG, States appeared first on Vanguard News .
